name: refactor_yolo_api_to_sqlalchemy
prompt: refactor the api to use sqlalchemy
expected_output: The agent creates services/yolo/models.py with SQLAlchemy ORM models PredictionSession and DetectionObject, creates services/yolo/db.py with engine, SessionLocal, get_db, SQLite default and Postgres configuration via environment variables, updates services/yolo/app.py to use SQLAlchemy sessions and FastAPI Depends(get_db), updates services/yolo/requirements.txt to include SQLAlchemy and a Postgres driver, preserves all existing endpoint paths and response shapes, removes sqlite3 imports and sqlite3.connect usage from the YOLO app code, and runs pytest tests/ or reports test failures with details.
assertions: PredictionSession and DetectionObject ORM classes are defined
services/yolo/app.py uses Depends(get_db) or otherwise injects SQLAlchemy sessions
POST /predict response still includes prediction_uid, detection_count, labels, and time_took
GET /prediction/{uid} response still includes uid, timestamp, original_image, predicted_image, and detection_objects
Postgres is configurable with environment variables

name: add_recent_predictions_endpoint
prompt: add an endpoint GET /predictions/recent that returns the 10 most recent sessions
expected_output: The agent adds GET /predictions/recent using the SQLAlchemy data layer, queries PredictionSession ordered by timestamp descending, limits results to 10, returns the same session-style fields used by existing prediction endpoints, includes detection objects if consistent with existing session responses, does not use raw SQL or sqlite3, and adds or updates tests for the endpoint.
assertions: Response shape is consistent with existing prediction session responses

name: add_user_feedback_table
prompt: add a UserFeedback table to track user ratings per prediction
expected_output: The agent updates services/yolo/models.py with a UserFeedback SQLAlchemy ORM model linked to prediction_uid, creates any needed API helpers or endpoints only if requested by the existing project pattern, preserves existing endpoints and response shapes, updates table creation through SQLAlchemy metadata, avoids raw SQL and sqlite3, and adds tests for creating or querying feedback if an endpoint is added.
assertions: UserFeedback includes prediction_uid and rating fields
Existing PredictionSession and DetectionObject models remain intact
Existing endpoint response shapes are preserved
No raw sqlite3 usage is introduced
Tests or clear verification steps are provided

name: delete_prediction_by_uid
prompt: delete a prediction session and all its detection objects by uid
expected_output: The agent implements deletion through SQLAlchemy ORM so deleting a prediction session also deletes its related detection objects, either through ORM cascade or explicit SQLAlchemy deletes. It preserves existing endpoints unless adding a new DELETE endpoint is requested, returns appropriate 404 behavior when the uid does not exist, avoids raw SQL and sqlite3, and adds tests covering deletion and missing uid behavior.
assertions: DetectionObject rows for the prediction are deleted
Missing uid returns 404 if an endpoint is added
No raw DELETE SQL string is used for normal CRUD
Tests cover successful delete and missing uid

name: add_processing_time_column
prompt: add a column processing_time_ms to the prediction_sessions table
expected_output: The agent updates the SQLAlchemy PredictionSession model with processing_time_ms, stores prediction processing time during POST /predict, preserves the existing /predict response keys and existing read response shapes unless the user explicitly requests exposing the new field, avoids raw SQL and sqlite3, and adds or updates tests confirming the value is stored.
assertions: POST /predict stores processing time in the database
Existing read endpoint response shapes are not changed unless requested

name: postgres_configurable_backend
prompt: make the database backend configurable so we can use postgres in production
expected_output: The agent implements database backend selection in services/yolo/db.py using DB_BACKEND with SQLite as the default and PostgreSQL when DB_BACKEND=postgres. It uses DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, and DB_NAME environment variables, keeps SQLite working locally, adds a PostgreSQL driver dependency, does not hardcode secrets, and documents or tests both configurations.
assertions: Postgres URL uses DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD, DB_HOST, DB_PORT, and DB_NAME
Verification steps for SQLite and Postgres are provided
